ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: Place a set of set squares as shown in the figure, what is the degree measure of $\angle AOB$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure below: \\
From the diagram, we can see that $\angle 1=30^\circ$, $\angle 2=45^\circ$, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle 3=\angle 1+\angle 2=75^\circ$, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle AOB=180^\circ-\angle 3=\boxed{105^\circ}$,

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, there are two set squares placed on the same horizontal base. The left set square has a vertical side on the left, with the vertex labeled B, and the hypotenuse extends from B toward the lower right; the right set square has a vertical side on the right, with the vertex labeled A, and the hypotenuse extends from the lower left toward the upper right to A. The two hypotenuses intersect at O, and what is required is ∠AOB. Reasoning: Because the problem states they are set squares, the acute angle formed by the hypotenuse of the left set square and the horizontal base is 30°, and the acute angle formed by the hypotenuse OA of the right set square and the horizontal base is 45°. Therefore the small angle formed by the two hypotenuses below/to the right of O is 30° + 45° = 75°. This 75° angle and ∠AOB are a pair of adjacent supplementary angles formed by the same two intersecting straight lines, so ∠AOB = 180° - 75° = 105°.

Use the text cue that these are set squares to identify the left set square as giving a 30° angle between its slanted edge and the horizontal base, and the right set square as giving a 45° angle between its slanted edge OA and the horizontal base. The small angle between the two slanted edges on the lower/right side of O is therefore 30° + 45° = 75°. Since this 75° angle and angle AOB form a linear pair around the same two intersecting lines, angle AOB = 180° - 75° = 105°.

method.method_draft: First describe the diagram: the base is horizontal, ray OA lies along the rising slanted side of the right set square, and ray OB lies along the slanted side of the left set square going up-left from O to B. Assign each ray a direction relative to the positive horizontal base. Because the right set square is a 45° set square, ray OA has direction 45° above the positive horizontal. Because the left set square has its hypotenuse making 30° with the horizontal but ray OB points up-left, ray OB has direction 180° - 30° = 150°. The angle from OA to OB is then 150° - 45° = 105°, so angle AOB measures 105°.

Thus ray OA points up-right along the slanted side of the right set square, while ray OB points up-left along the slanted side of the left set square. Reasoning: Take the horizontal base direction to the right as 0°. The right set square is a 45° set square, so ray OA has direction 45° above the positive horizontal. The left set square has its hypotenuse making 30° with the horizontal, but ray OB points up-left, so its direction is 180° - 30° = 150°. Therefore, angle AOB is the difference between these directions: 150° - 45° = 105°.
